name: Mahli
overview: Mahli was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Mushi. He belonged to the Merarite family line, descended from Merari, one of Levi's sons. This places Mahli within the Levitical clan responsible for specific duties related to the Tabernacle, according to biblical genealogies.
namesAndTitles: The name Mahli is a proper name mentioned in Scripture and is possibly derived from a root meaning 'shrewd' or 'cunning.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a typical Hebrew personal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mahli as the son of Mushi, and it is inferred that Shemer was his father, linking him firmly within the Levitical genealogy. Beyond these connections, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mahli's significance lies in his place within the Levitical lineage, particularly among the Merarites, who were entrusted with specific responsibilities in the service of the Tabernacle. His identification as a descendant of Mushi highlights the organized structure God established for the tribe of Levi, emphasizing faithful service and lineage purity. Though not prominent in narrative events, Mahli represents the faithful continuation of God's covenantal people through the Levitical priestly families.
